stories.notes: Story has zero acceptance criteria and covers a complex multi-platform (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature in the CMS. Needs openspec first to elaborate AC, define technical depth around real-time rendering and platform-specific preview behavior, then speckit to harden testability, security (e.g. iframe sandboxing, XSS in preview content), and edge cases (network latency, concurrent edits, unsupported content types). No existing spec or hand-curated flag detected; no dependencies blocking this phase.

agentContributions.notes: Novel story: Contentstack Live Preview integration. Attachment point is useContent hook (236 callers) and ContentstackContext provider. Verification criteria derived from description claims: real-time updates, useContent integration, 236+ components auto-reflecting changes. All VCs are black-box observable and stop at the Contentstack service boundary (mocked).

Openspec produced an empty acceptanceCriteria array. I built the full list from scratch based on the story title/description (Contentstack Live Preview integration) and openspec's notes (useContent hook, ContentstackContext, 236 callers, real-time updates, service boundary). ACs 1-3 cover the core functional claims. ACs 4-5 and 6, 12, 13 cover error handling and reconnection. ACs 7, 8, 14 cover edge cases (rapid updates, malformed payloads, cross-contamination). AC-9 covers XSS security. AC-10 covers accessibility. AC-11 covers data exposure. I could not read source files (useContent, ContentstackContext, etc.) so criteria are based on documented behavior claims — if file contents reveal architectural details that invalidate any AC, those should be adjusted during implementation review.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Openspec failed its primary responsibility: the story had zero acceptance criteria and openspec produced an empty AC array despite noting it derived verification criteria from description claims. Speckit compensated by building 13 ACs from scratch, but this represents a workflow inversion — speckit should have hardened existing ACs, not authored them. The ACs are unverified against source code (speckit explicitly could not read useContent, ContentstackContext, or other relevant files), so architectural validity is uncertain. No story split was considered despite the story spanning three platforms (GO, UP, MX), which likely warrants decomposition. Security and edge-case coverage (XSS, reconnection, rapid updates, cross-contamination) added by speckit is meaningful and non-overlapping with openspec's architectural context notes, but the collaborative pipeline did not function as designed. Human review needed to validate ACs against actual source architecture and assess whether a multi-platform split is required.
